text:
Christopher Columbus

Frederick stared at the bubbling cauldron, the scent of sulfur and rare herbs filling the air. The runes on the altar seemed to pulse in time with his heartbeat. He had spent decades hunting for this moment, sacrificing friendships, wealth, and peace of mind. But as he looked at the final ingredient—a drop of his own blood required to activate the potion—he hesitated.

The draft from the hidden chamber grew stronger, carrying with it the faint sound of the world above: the wind in the trees, the distant cry of a bird, the rustle of leaves. It was the sound of life, fleeting and fragile. He realized that immortality would mean watching everyone he loved turn to dust while he remained unchanged, a ghost in a world that moved on without him.

Instead of adding the final drop, Frederick picked up the parchment. He held it over the flame of the brazier. The runes curled and blackened, the secret to eternal life dissolving into ash. He didn't destroy the book entirely; he closed it and placed it back on the altar, but he broke the seal that had guarded it. He left the chamber, locking the door behind him, not to keep others out, but to keep the temptation in. He walked out into the sunlight, ready to live his remaining years fully, knowing that the end was what gave life its meaning.
